name: GO-STOP (GODORI)
description: Go Stop is a Korean flower-card fishing game in which players capture matching month cards, build scoring combinations, and choose whether to stop for payout or go on for higher risk and reward.

content.text: Go Stop is a Korean flower-card fishing game in which players capture matching month cards, build scoring combinations, and choose whether to stop for payout or go on for higher risk and reward.
Go Stop developed in Korea from Japanese flower-card traditions and became the best-known Korean hwatu fishing game.
2 or 3 active players; larger groups may rotate players between hands.
48 hwatu cards (12 months x 4 cards), with optional jokers depending on table rules.
Score sheet or chips for multi-hand accounting.
Two-player game: 10 cards each and 8 to table. Three-player game: 7 cards each and 6 to table. Remaining cards form stock.

items.text: Matgo (Two-Player): Two-player rules use different deal size and commonly higher stop threshold than three-player play.
No-Joker Table: Play with the base 48-card deck and no joker cards or joker-specific bonuses.
